en: Many think Jose Rizal wrote Noli Me Tangere in Manila, but he actually finished it in Berlin, Germany.
Although many celebrate July 4, Philippine Independence was actually declared by Emilio Aguinaldo on June 12, 1898.
Many believe the rare Waling-waling is the national flower, but the official Philippine national flower is actually the Sampaguita.
Many children think the President makes laws, but the Legislative branch, called Congress, actually creates Philippine legislation.
People often think Igorot is a single tribe, but it is actually an umbrella term for several distinct Cordillera ethnolinguistic groups.
Many think Tagalog is the only native language, but the Philippines actually has over one hundred distinct indigenous languages.
Many think the MassKara Festival is a solemn event, but it is actually a vibrant celebration of smiles.
Many believe Fe del Mundo invented the standard electric incubator, but she actually created an innovative bamboo incubator.
Many think Andres Bonifacio was the first president, but Emilio Aguinaldo actually served as the first Philippine president.
Filipinos sometimes think utang na loob means paying a financial debt, but it actually refers to a deep moral debt of gratitude.
Many think the flag's eight sun rays represent islands, but they actually symbolize the first eight provinces that revolted.
Many assume Juan Luna painted the Spoliarium in Manila, but he actually created this masterpiece in Rome, Italy.
